report.incidentSummary: During evening peak traffic on 2026-09-16 starting at ~14:35 UTC (20:05 IST), users experienced 20-30 second assistant response times and occasional failed responses. Traffic to assistant-orchestrator rose to ~34-36 req/s (~2040-2160 req/min), which exceeded llm-provider's quota limit of 1500 requests per minute. llm-provider began returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. assistant-orchestrator retried failed calls up to 2 times with backoffs up to 8 seconds, inflating p95 response time to ~25 seconds. When all retries were exhausted, it returned fallback messages (error rate ~4.7%). A prompt update deployed at 14:42 UTC occurred after the onset and was not the cause.
report.rootCauseStatement: assistant-orchestrator traffic during the evening peak (~34 req/s = ~2,040 req/min) exceeded llm-provider's provisioned request-rate quota (1,500 requests per minute). llm-provider throttled requests with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests starting at 14:35:07 UTC, triggering assistant-orchestrator's backoff retry loop (up to 3 attempts), which inflated p95 latency to 24-26 seconds and produced fallback error responses when retries were exhausted.

hypotheses.cause: Evening peak chat volume (~34 req/s = ~2040 req/min) exceeded llm-provider's rate limit quota (1500 requests per minute), triggering HTTP 429 errors and orchestrator retry backoffs that pushed latency to 20-30s.
hypotheses.rationale: Supported by timing and direct log and metric evidence: request rate exceeded 1500 req/min starting at evening peak; 429 errors explicitly state 'quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500' starting at 14:35:07 UTC on version 0.42.0; orchestrator backoff retries caused 20-30s latency and fallback failures when retries were exhausted.

hypotheses.cause: Prompt template deployment (CHG-48222) caused token bloat leading to latency regression.
hypotheses.rationale: Ruled out by timing and metrics: the incident started at 14:35:07 UTC on version 0.42.0, whereas CHG-48222 was deployed at 14:42:00 UTC (v0.43.0). Furthermore, tokens per minute and input tokens per request remained steady, and the rate limit error was specifically on requests per minute, not tokens.

hypotheses.cause: Downstream dependency degradation in user-context-service, knowledge-index, compliance-filter, or cache.
hypotheses.rationale: Ruled out: cache hit rates remained 93-95%, and latencies for knowledge-index (~90ms), compliance-filter (~120ms), and user-context-service (~195ms) remained healthy and normal throughout the incident.

facts.statement: A prompt template update (CHG-48222) was deployed to assistant-orchestrator (v0.42.0 -> v0.43.0) at 2026-09-16T14:42:00.000Z.

assistant-orchestrator p95 latency rose from ~7,300 ms at 14:35 UTC to 23,266 ms at 14:40 UTC and remained at 24,000-26,000 ms; llm_latency_p95_ms similarly jumped from ~5,700 ms to 21,000-23,000 ms starting at 14:36 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count jumped from 0 to 18.2/min at 14:36 UTC and peaked at 72.5/min; retry_count surged from ~2/min to 20-68/min; error_rate rose from ~0.5% to 4.7%.

Starting at 14:35:07.794Z on version 0.42.0, assistant-orchestrator logged hundreds of warnings: 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500); retrying in #s', and errors: 'conversation failed: llm-provider 429 after 3 attempts; returned fallback message'.

App traffic increased during the evening peak starting around 13:30 UTC (19:00 IST), with assistant-orchestrator request_rate jumping from ~20 req/s (~1200 req/min) to ~34-36 req/s (~2040-2160 req/min).

assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min remained steady between 270,000 and 350,000 tokens/min throughout 14:20-15:00 UTC, with input token lengths per conversation turn remaining consistent (~2,000-5,000 tokens) before and after CHG-48222.
assistant-orchestrator depends on llm-provider with timeout 25,000 ms and 2 retries (3 total attempts).
Other dependencies (cache, compliance-filter, knowledge-index, user-context-service) operated normally with expected latencies and cache hit rates of 93-95% throughout the incident window.

inferences.statement: During off-peak daytime hours, assistant request rates of ~20 req/s (~1200 req/min) stayed comfortably below the 1500 req/min quota limit; evening peak volume (~34 req/s) breached the quota.
The 20-30 second latency symptom is directly caused by assistant-orchestrator's retry backoff loop (up to 2 retries with 3-8s sleep per retry on HTTP 429), culminating in timeout or fallback failure.

assumptions.statement: llm-provider enforces rate limits using a sliding window or token bucket algorithm that accommodated brief bursts until sustained peak traffic depleted the quota at 14:35 UTC.

timeline.event: Evening peak traffic begins; assistant-orchestrator request_rate jumps from ~20 req/s to ~34 req/s (~2040 req/min).
First HTTP 429 rate limit error received from llm-provider on version 0.42.0 ('quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500').
assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms begins sharp rise (9,632 ms at 14:36, reaching ~24,000 ms by 14:40) due to 429 backoff retries.
Conversations begin failing with fallback messages after exhausting 3 retry attempts against llm-provider 429s.
Support duty manager files incident INC-9062 reporting assistant taking 20-30s and failing.
CHG-48222 deployed assistant-orchestrator v0.43.0 (prompt template update); 429 errors continue unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Clear, unambiguous log and metric evidence directly shows HTTP 429 quota exhaustion ('limit=1500 requests per minute') from llm-provider starting at 14:35:07 UTC under evening peak load (~34 req/s = ~2040 req/min), with orchestrator backoff retries driving p95 latency to 24-26 seconds and fallback message returns. The prompt deployment at 14:42 UTC occurred after the incident onset and did not affect token metrics.

gaps.impact: Minimal; log messages explicitly quote the exact limit value ('limit=1500 requests per minute') and quota failure reason.

recommendedActions.action: Request an immediate quota increase with llm-provider to at least 3,000 requests per minute to safely support peak evening traffic (~35-40 req/s plus headroom).
recommendedActions.rationale: The current 1,500 req/min limit is insufficient for peak assistant traffic (~2,040 req/min), causing sustained 429 throttling and degraded user experience.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify rate_limited_count drops to zero and 429 responses cease in assistant-orchestrator logs during peak hours.

recommendedActions.action: Tune assistant-orchestrator retry policy for HTTP 429 responses (e.g. fast-fail or circuit break instead of multiple high-latency backoff retries when quota is exhausted).
recommendedActions.rationale: Repeated 3-8s retries for hard quota limits delay response times to 25+ seconds, degrading user experience for all throttled users.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate upstream 429 responses in staging and verify responses fail quickly with fallback rather than blocking for 25 seconds.

recommendedActions.action: Implement client-side rate limiting or request queuing on api-gateway for /v1/assistant/chat matched to upstream LLM quotas.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents uncoordinated storm of requests hitting the LLM provider when traffic surges above agreed partner tiers.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm gateway throttles excess requests gracefully with 429 and Retry-After headers before overloading backend services.

report.justification: Investigation was concluded with high confidence because direct metrics and logs established the onset time, exact error code (HTTP 429), quota reason ('quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500'), and ruled out the deployment CHG-48222 by timing (14:42 UTC deploy vs 14:35:07 UTC error onset on v0.42.0) and token metrics.

# Investigation report: Assistant very slow this evening

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** budget_tool_calls · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** baseline agent
> Honesty check: reported conclusive although the run stopped (budget_tool_calls) without critic acceptance; the report gives a justification

## Summary
During evening peak traffic on 2026-09-16 starting at ~14:35 UTC (20:05 IST), users experienced 20-30 second assistant response times and occasional failed responses. Traffic to assistant-orchestrator rose to ~34-36 req/s (~2040-2160 req/min), which exceeded llm-provider's quota limit of 1500 requests per minute. llm-provider began returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. assistant-orchestrator retried failed calls up to 2 times with backoffs up to 8 seconds, inflating p95 response time to ~25 seconds. When all retries were exhausted, it returned fallback messages (error rate ~4.7%). A prompt update deployed at 14:42 UTC occurred after the onset and was not the cause.

**Root cause:** assistant-orchestrator traffic during the evening peak (~34 req/s = ~2,040 req/min) exceeded llm-provider's provisioned request-rate quota (1,500 requests per minute). llm-provider throttled requests with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests starting at 14:35:07 UTC, triggering assistant-orchestrator's backoff retry loop (up to 3 attempts), which inflated p95 latency to 24-26 seconds and produced fallback error responses when retries were exhausted.
